sourceInputs.outputBound: maxKnownOutputBytes = template bytes minus its {name} tokens plus 20 bytes per placeholder (the longest Lua 5.1 tostring, %.14g, of a finite value >= 0); every current value is below the 254-byte result limit; unknown slots render as ?

runtimeContract.language: Lua 5.1; Nexus.toc ## Interface: 30300; addon identity Nexus; load order data/LocalizationEnglish.lua, data/LocalizationPacks.lua, core/Localization.lua (Nexus.toc lines 13-15)
runtimeContract.keys: 3 to 64 bytes; two or more dot-separated segments of lower-case ASCII letters, digits and _, each starting with a letter (ValidKey, core/Localization.lua:162)
runtimeContract.text: 1 to 256 bytes; well-formed shortest-form UTF-8 of Unicode scalar values only (WellFormedUtf8, :182); at least one byte outside ASCII whitespace 9-13 and 32; no control byte 0-31 or 127 and no | (124), so no colour, link or texture markup and no newline; no normalization (ValidText, :211)
runtimeContract.staticText: shown exactly as stored; never formatted; a static key cannot be used with Format (wrong_key_kind)
runtimeContract.templatedText: only keys with a code-owned schema (SCHEMAS, :232) are templates; today only readout.charge_counts with fields banish, reroll, freeze, each exactly once in any order; {{ and }} are literal braces; % and every other byte are literal; {1}, {name:d}, unknown, missing or repeated names and lone braces invalidate the template; a template key cannot be shown as static text (format_requires_arguments)
runtimeContract.countArguments: each slot is exactly {known = true, value = N} with N a finite whole number >= 0 shown with tostring, or exactly {known = false} shown as ?; 0 is a known count, never unknown; substitution is one pass
runtimeContract.resultLimit: CHARGE_RESULT_LIMIT = MAX_TEXT_BYTES - 2 = 254 bytes, so the consumer's " ~" estimate marker keeps the row within 256; an over-limit candidate falls back to the English template; an over-limit English result is the safe unavailable status; a result is never cut
runtimeContract.unavailableStatus: This status cannot be shown right now.
runtimeContract.unavailableStatusNote: English-only safe status for an invalid or unknown key, a template used as static text, a static key used as a template and invalid arguments; it is never translated by a pack
runtimeContract.packs: a pack is adopted only when it is a plain table with a valid autonym (text contract, at most 64 bytes) and a plain entries table of at most 64 entries; otherwise it is refused and not offered; an entry is copied only for an existing English static key with valid text, or an English template key whose text compiles under the same schema; other entries are left out and counted rejected; a candidate never adds a key
runtimeContract.activeLanguage: InitializeActiveLanguage(id) is honoured once per Lua session (:679); an ID without an adopted pack, an absent value or the Automatic preference gives English in this build (ResolveAutomatic, :647, has no evidenced client alias); a changed preference applies at the next reload or login
runtimeContract.fallback: Text/Format with an omitted pack use the active pack; a missing or invalid candidate (or Format output over the limit) yields the exact English text or English template with the same arguments, source base, and a counted reason (missing_candidate, invalid_candidate, unsupported_pack, output_limit); Resolve and FormatResolve are pure supplied-pack functions; Diagnostics keeps at most 8 distinct invalid or unknown keys
runtimeContract.capFailureMode: an English base above 64 entries adopts nothing (oversized; every key then answers the unavailable status); a pack above 64 entries is refused as a whole (tests/prototype/terminology.lua:335 and :342 exercise 64 accepted and 65 failing closed)
runtimeContract.validatorMirror: tools/l10n_catalog.py mirrors the same byte limits (_MAX_KEY_BYTES, _MAX_TEXT_BYTES, _MAX_BASE_ENTRIES = 64, _MAX_NAME_BYTES, _MAX_LANGUAGES = 16) and the one charge schema with limit 254 (lines 432-440)
runtimeContract.notProvenByThisContract: native glyph, font, locale, layout, input or visibility behaviour
